title: 2025 Monthly Atmospheric Temp & Monsoon Cycle (Jan–Dec 2025)
source: NASA GPM IMERG v07B & NASA POWER MERRA-2 Reanalysis
coords: LAT: 12.97° N | LON: 77.59° E (SOUTH ASIA MONSOON CORE)
theoryOverview: NASA's Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) Dual-frequency Precipitation Radar (DPR) and MERRA-2 reanalysis track the complete 12-month thermodynamic cycle of 2025. As pre-monsoon solar insolation heats the Indian subcontinent from March to May, a deep thermal low-pressure trough forms, drawing cross-equatorial moisture winds that erupt into extreme convective rainfall between June and September.

records.explanation: Jan 2025 Winter Baseline: Cool 23.4°C continental air mass with dry 12.5mm northeast winter trade winds.
records.theory: Subtropical jet stream sits south of the Himalayas; high atmospheric stability suppresses cloud vertical development.

records.explanation: Feb 2025 Early Vernal Warming: Clear skies drive a +2.4°C jump to 25.8°C with light 18.2mm western disturbances.
records.theory: Increasing solar zenith angle begins heating the Deccan plateau, gradually raising baseline acoustic pitch.

records.explanation: Mar 2025 Equinox Heat Buildup: Land surface temperature climbs to 28.9°C; localized 29.4mm pre-monsoon thundershowers.
records.theory: Strong sensible heat flux from dry soil creates afternoon convective instability (Kalbaishakhi/Mango showers).

records.explanation: Apr 2025 Thermal Low Formation: Intense 31.6°C heatwave establishes the continental heat-low; 54.0mm convective bursts.
records.theory: NASA MERRA-2 records peak surface skin temperatures, setting up the land-sea barometric pressure gradient.

records.explanation: May 2025 Pre-Monsoon Peak: Yearly thermal high of 32.8°C! Cross-equatorial Somali Jet initiates 118.5mm pre-monsoon surge.
records.theory: Latent heat release in the Bay of Bengal primes the troposphere for the Southwest Monsoon onset.

records.explanation: Jun 2025 Southwest Monsoon Onset: Rainfall doubles to 245.0mm as dense cumulonimbus clouds cool air to 29.4°C.
records.theory: GPM IMERG microwave radiometers detect deep liquid/ice water paths across the Western Ghats and central plains.

records.explanation: Jul 2025 Peak Monsoon Cloudburst: Maximum 342.6mm deluge! High-frequency raindrop arpeggio & storm siren engage.
records.theory: Active Monsoon Trough + Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO) phase alignment produces extreme daily precipitation rates.

records.explanation: Aug 2025 Core Monsoon Sustain: 318.4mm heavy rainfall fueled by Bay of Bengal low-pressure depressions.
records.theory: Warm sea surface temperatures feed continuous moisture transport inland, maintaining high acoustic harmonic density.

records.explanation: Sep 2025 Late-Monsoon Withdrawal Phase: 210.8mm intense retreating storms with 28.3°C humid warmth.
records.theory: Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) begins southward migration as northern hemisphere solar heating wanes.

records.explanation: Oct 2025 Northeast Monsoon Transition: Wind reversal brings 142.0mm coastal cyclonic rains and 27.6°C temperatures.
records.theory: Coriolis-deflected northeast trade winds pick up moisture over the warm Bay of Bengal, impacting southern peninsular India.

records.explanation: Nov 2025 Post-Monsoon Cooling: Temperature drops to 25.4°C with 68.5mm residual tropical depression rainfall.
records.theory: Radiative cooling accelerates over the continent; synth frequency steps down into warm mid-range harmonics.

records.explanation: Dec 2025 Winter Solstice Stabilization: Calm 23.8°C and 24.0mm dry winter regime completes the 2025 annual cycle.
records.theory: High-pressure anticyclonic circulation re-establishes over South Asia, returning the sonification to its calm baseline.
